findings.title: Release test timeout was shorter than its one-hour contract
findings.proposed_fix: Use a 3600-second timeout per release suite.
findings.retest_evidence: 3 Sep 2026, isolated worktree retest/f500-003 off origin/main@2f7fdc5c, commit 5f88acd1 (TEST_SUITE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 1800->3600 only - an unrelated gate_nav_verified 'unmeasured'-handling change found bundled into the same uncommitted diff in the shared worktree was deliberately excluded as out of this finding's scope). Regression test confirmed the defect first: tests/test_verify_test_suite_timeout.py failed pre-fix (assert all(timeout==3600...) -> False), passed post-fix (1/1). Root cause of the regression traced one level: an earlier fix (commit b465bd1f, 28 Aug 2026) had already set this constant to 3600 with the same regression test, but candidate_base 2f7fdc5c carries 1800 again - lost via a merge, not re-investigated further here. SECOND closure test ('Full database-backed verifier', i.e. `python scripts/verify.py --gate tests --require-db`) could NOT be completed in this session: three attempts (two backgrounded run_in_background invocations and one direct redirect-to-file invocation, each 40-90+ minutes) all terminated at the harness/shell level (empty output files, exit 127 or 255) rather than at the test level - `tasklist` confirmed genuine pytest worker processes alive and consuming 800MB-1.8GB RAM mid-run each time, so this reads as a session/background-duration ceiling in the interactive tool harness on this Windows host, not a defect in the fix or a test failure. Recommend rerunning `python scripts/verify.py --require-db` (or just `--gate tests --require-db`) either in CI or as a detached, non-interactively-monitored process with a longer-lived shell before marking this verified - do not treat the unit-level pass alone as satisfying both named closure tests.

findings.title: Six documented governance/AI-safety gates exist as scripts but are never registered in build_gates(), so they never run
findings.original_evidence: 3 Sep 2026, docs-audit worktree (branch docs/claude-md-drift-audit, base 2f7fdc5c): `grep -oE '^\s*Gate\("[a-z0-9-]+"' scripts/verify.py | sort -u | wc -l` -> 44, not the 67 docs/DELIVERY_CONTRACT.md claimed. `grep -rn "role-gate-coverage|ai-evidence-rules|ai-tool-guard|ai-untrusted-content|ai-approval-honoured|evidence-contract" scripts/verify.py` -> no matches. The six scripts (scripts/check_evidence_contract.py, scripts/check_role_gate_coverage.py, scripts/check_ai_evidence_rules.py, scripts/check_ai_tool_guard.py, scripts/check_ai_untrusted_content.py, scripts/check_ai_approval_honoured.py) exist on disk and are not wrapped in a Gate(...) entry in build_gates(), so none run as part of `python scripts/verify.py`, CI, or anywhere else found in the repository. Re-deriving DELIVERY_CONTRACT.md's role-to-gate table from the 44 gates that actually exist found 12 of 15 roles measure 0 real gates (including AI/ML architect, product architect, business architect, service designer, data/evidence analyst, integration architect), not the 1-8 the table claimed - because those roles' tags (ai, architecture, process, product, journey, business, handoff, evidence, integration, rendered, wayfinding, content) are not carried by any currently-registered gate. CLAUDE.md separately claimed 88/98 units of ratchet debt for design_tokens/raw_sql_tenancy that both currently measure 0, and documented 19 gates against the real 44 - both were also corrected in the same pass (see branch docs/claude-md-drift-audit for the full diff, not yet merged).
findings.required_fix: Register the six scripts as Gate(...) entries in scripts/verify.py's build_gates(), each with a Proven-against: line per DELIVERY_CONTRACT.md Rule 2 (reintroduce the defect, confirm red, restore, confirm green) before trusting them in the release gate - do not wire them in unproven, per this same document's own account of a gate it built and deliberately did not ship because it had false positives. Re-derive and correct docs/DELIVERY_CONTRACT.md's role-to-gate table once the real tag set is known.
findings.retest_evidence: 3 Sep 2026: registry contract passed; five root-aware seeded red/green proof cases plus checker-provenance test passed (6 tests); verifier gates passed evidence-contract 29<=29, role-gate-coverage 7<=7, and all four AI gates 0<=0. Final CI retest remains required on the release SHA.
closure_tests: grep -oE '^\s*Gate\("(evidence-contract|role-gate-coverage|ai-evidence-rules|ai-tool-guard|ai-untrusted-content|ai-approval-honoured)"' scripts/verify.py must match all six
Each of the six gates has a documented Proven-against case reproduced: reintroduce the named defect, gate goes red; restore, gate goes green

findings.title: .gitignore blanket-ignores scripts/check_*.py, requiring a manual allowlist line per permanent gate - the likely root mechanism behind F500-008
findings.original_evidence: 3 Sep 2026, worktree gov-gates (branch feat/docs-drift-and-check-registration, base e74bd8ec): creating two new checker scripts (scripts/check_docs_drift.py, scripts/check_unregistered_checks.py) and running `git add` showed 'The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files'. `git check-ignore -v` traced both to .gitignore:196 `scripts/check_*.py`. The surrounding comment already documents one prior casualty: 'these globs are why DESIGN.md can reference a check_token_migration.py pre-commit hook that is absent from the repository - a permanent quality gate was named like a throwaway and got ignored out of existence.' Every one of the 70 check_*.py scripts currently tracked required its own `!scripts/check_X.py` negation line added by hand; the default is to silently drop a new one unless the author notices and force-adds it.
findings.required_fix: This finding was fixed rather than left open, since it was a one-line addition needed anyway to commit the two new gates: negation lines added for both new scripts. The systemic direction (default-ignore + manual allowlist for a class of file meant to be permanent) is unchanged and worth inverting - default-track scripts/check_*.py and ignore only files matching a genuinely-scratch naming convention (scripts/check_*_scratch.py, or similar) - but that broader change is out of scope of this fix and not attempted here.
findings.retest_evidence: 3 Sep 2026: both new scripts committed successfully after the negation lines were added (commit 037490fc); `git ls-files scripts/check_*.py | wc -l` -> 72 (70 pre-existing + 2 new), confirming both are now tracked.
closure_tests: git check-ignore -v scripts/check_docs_drift.py scripts/check_unregistered_checks.py must report no match
git ls-files scripts/check_*.py includes both new scripts

findings.original_evidence: 3 Sep 2026: `python scripts/benchmark_scale.py --i-know-this-is-not-prod ...` exited before any writes with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'app' because direct script execution placed scripts/, not the repository root, on sys.path.
